_about.purpose: Quality gate for tests/test_matching_benchmark.py. The benchmark asserts the current ranker is no worse than every number in 'metrics'. This is a regression gate, not a target.
_about.dataset: tests/fixtures/eval_jobs_real.json (version 7, 190 real listings, rebuild with `python -m tests.build_eval_dataset`)
_about.regenerate: Only when a change is intended to move these numbers: run tests/test_matching_benchmark.py::test_report_measured_metrics with -s, read the printed tables, and update the values deliberately.
_about.recall_is_not_comparable_to_version_5: Version 5 held 7 'relevant' rows; version 7 holds 66, selected on job family, location and stated experience bar alone - never on whether the candidate's skills match. Recall therefore measures something harder and its value fell from 0.8571 to 0.4091 without the ranker getting worse. The precision figures, the false-positive rate and the per-row facts are the comparable numbers.
_about.why_recall_is_low: Measured, not assumed: of 66 suitable rows, none is filtered incorrectly, and those that miss the review band sit at 40-60 because skills carry 35% of the weight and almost no listing in this pool publishes a requirements list, so skills are inferred and capped at 75. A listing whose inferred skills the candidate lacks is genuinely a weaker match, so this was left alone rather than tuned: raising the skills score to chase recall would be tuning against the benchmark and would cost the precision figures below.
_about.high_confidence_never_fires: Across all 190 real listings, 0 earn 'high' confidence, because the gate needs a published requirements list and these employers rarely publish one. The label is effectively unreachable on real data and is recorded here so the gap stays visible rather than being mistaken for a healthy distribution.

per_family_note: -1.0 means the metric has no rows of that kind and is undefined. software_general and frontend contain no unsuitable rows, so their false-positive rate is undefined rather than perfect. Non-target rows carry no family of their own and only their false-positive rate is meaningful. Every family except software_general has a mean suitable score just below the candidate's own 65 threshold, which is why their recall is low while their false-positive rate is zero.
confidence_calibration_note: A medium-confidence row is suitable 56% of the time against 19% for a low-confidence row, and carries higher evidence coverage (0.90 against 0.64). The label therefore carries real information and is worth showing to the user. This is the check that would fail if confidence were decorative.
